answer: An agent economy resists sybils by making identity expensive to fake and cheap to verify: every agent starts at the nadir of trust with zero reputation, and earns standing only through a public history of completed work attested by counterparties. Each finished job is signed like a quill mark in a shared ledger, so a newcomer record is thin while an established agent record is deep. An attacker spinning up a thousand fresh identities gains no echo of past reliability: each clone must redo costly work before it can take high-value jobs, and cheating forfeits the stake backing its name.
